title: Boeing FY2022 10-K — Legal proceedings disclosure policy (reasonably possible losses in excess of recorded amounts)
key_points: Boeing states that, based on current information, it believes the outcome of legal proceedings, claims, and government disputes and investigations will not have a material effect on its financial position, results of operations or cash flows.

Where it is reasonably possible that losses in excess of recorded amounts will be incurred, Boeing discloses either the amount or range of reasonably possible losses in excess of such amounts, or, where no amount or range can be reasonably estimated, the reasons why no estimate can be made.
raw_excerpt: based upon current information, that the outcome of any such legal proceeding, claim, or government dispute and investigation will not have a material effect on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows. Where it is reasonably possible that we will incur losses in excess of recorded amounts in connection with any of the matters set forth below, we will disclose either the amount or range of reasonably possible losses in excess of such amounts or, where no such amount or range can be reasonably estimated, the reasons why no such estimate can be made.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K — 737 MAX accident litigation: DOJ DPA, shareholder derivative settlement ($219), SEC civil penalty ($200)
key_points: Multiple legal actions have been filed against Boeing as a result of the October 29, 2018 Lion Air Flight 610 accident and the March 10, 2019 Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 accident.

During 2021 Boeing entered into a Deferred Prosecution Agreement with the U.S. Department of Justice that resolved DOJ's previously disclosed investigation into the evaluation of the 737 MAX by the FAA.
A proposed settlement with plaintiffs in a shareholder derivative lawsuit resulted in the Company receiving $219 (millions) in the second quarter of 2022.

In September 2022 Boeing settled a previously disclosed SEC investigation related to the 737 MAX accidents and consented to a civil penalty, resulting in an earnings charge of $200 (millions) paid in October 2022.

Boeing states it cannot reasonably estimate a range of loss, if any, not covered by available insurance that it may incur as a result of any remaining pending lawsuits or other matters related to the accidents and the 737 MAX.
raw_excerpt: Multiple legal actions have been filed against us as a result of the October 29, 2018 accident of Lion Air Flight 610 and the March 10, 2019 accident of Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302. During 2021, we entered into (i) a Deferred Prosecution Agreement with the U.S. Department of Justice that resolved the Department of Justice's previously disclosed investigation into us regarding the evaluation of the 737 MAX by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) as well as (ii) a proposed settlement with plaintiffs in a shareholder derivative lawsuit that resulted in the Company receiving $219 in the second quarter of 2022. In September 2022, we settled a previously disclosed investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission related to the 737 MAX accidents and consented to a civil penalty, which resulted in an earnings charge of $200 that was paid in October 2022. We cannot reasonably estimate a range of loss, if any, not covered by available insurance that we may incur as a result of any remaining pending lawsuits or other matters related to the accidents and the 737 MAX.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K — Embraer joint venture termination arbitration
key_points: In 2019 Boeing agreed with Embraer S.A. to establish joint ventures, including acquiring an 80 percent ownership stake in Embraer's commercial aircraft and services operations for $4,200 (millions).

In 2020 Boeing exercised its contractual right to terminate the agreements based on Embraer's failure to meet certain required closing conditions; Embraer disputes the termination and the dispute is currently in arbitration.
Boeing states it cannot reasonably estimate a range of loss, if any, that may result from the arbitration, which it expected to be completed in late 2023 or early 2024.
raw_excerpt: During 2019, we entered into agreements with Embraer S.A. (Embraer) to establish joint ventures that included the commercial aircraft and services operations of Embraer, of which we were expected to acquire an 80 percent ownership stake for $4,200 ... In 2020, we exercised our contractual right to terminate these agreements based on Embraer's failure to meet certain required closing conditions. Embraer has disputed our right to terminate the agreements, and the dispute is currently in arbitration. We cannot reasonably estimate a range of loss, if any, that may result from the arbitration, which we currently expect to be completed in late 2023 or early 2024.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K — Note 13 Accrued Liabilities and 737 MAX grounding customer concessions liability
key_points: Accrued liabilities at December 31, 2022 included '737 MAX grounding customer concessions and other considerations' of $1,864 million, down from $2,940 million at December 31, 2021.
Total accrued liabilities were $21,581 million at December 31, 2022 versus $18,455 million at December 31, 2021.
The $1.9 billion liability balance at December 31, 2022 comprises $1.6 billion of contracted customer concessions and other liabilities plus $0.3 billion still subject to negotiation with customers.
The contracted amount includes $0.8 billion expected to be liquidated by lower customer delivery payments, $0.7 billion expected to be paid in cash, and $0.1 billion in other concessions.
Of the cash payments to customers, $0.1 billion is expected to be paid in 2023 and the remaining $0.6 billion in future years.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K — Note 13 environmental remediation: high end of reasonably possible range exceeds recorded liability by $1,058 million
key_points: Recorded environmental liabilities represent management's best estimate or the low end of a range of reasonably possible costs, including operation and maintenance over periods of up to 30 years.
At December 31, 2022 and 2021, the high end of the estimated range of reasonably possible remediation costs exceeded recorded liabilities by $1,058 million and $1,094 million, respectively.
There are some potential remediation obligations where the costs of remediation cannot be reasonably estimated.
The environmental accrual balance was $752 million at December 31, 2022 versus $605 million at December 31, 2021.

title: BOEING_2022_10K — Item 1 Business, 737 Program（FAA 认证与安全增强要求状态）
key_points: 737-7 与 737-10 机型当时正在接受 FAA 型号认证。
《2023 年综合拨款法》修订了 ACSAA 第 116 条，使 2020 年 12 月 27 日之前提交的原始或修订型号认证申请（含 737-7 与 737-10）不再受第 116 条机组告警（crew alerting）规范的约束。
在 FAA 颁发 737-10 型号合格证满一年之后，任何新的 737 MAX 飞机必须包含特定安全增强措施才能获得 FAA 原始适航认证。
波音已为相关安全增强改装成本计提准备，并表示不预期该成本重大。
截至 2022 年 12 月 31 日，库存中有 27 架 737-7 与 3 架 737-10；订单储备（backlog）中有 236 架 737-7 与 720 架 737-10；737 MAX 累计已交付 1,033 架。
波音当时预计 737-7 于 2023 年取证交付，737-10 于 2023 年开始 FAA 认证试飞、2024 年首架交付。
raw_excerpt: The 737-7 and 737-10 models are currently going through FAA certification. The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 amended Section 116 of the ACSAA, such that applications for original or amended type certifications that were submitted to the FAA prior to December 27, 2020, including those of the 737-7 and 737-10, are no longer subject to the crew alerting specifications of Section 116. … We have provisioned for the estimated costs associated with the safety enhancements and do not expect those costs to be material.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Note 7 / MD&A: 787 and 777X program accounting disclosures
key_points: In the fourth quarter of 2021 Boeing recorded a $3,460 million reach-forward loss on the 787 program as a reduction to deferred production costs.

In April 2022 Boeing decided to pause production of the 777X-9 during 2022 and 2023; the pause is expected to result in abnormal production costs of approximately $1.5 billion, of which $325 million was expensed in 2022.
The 777X program had near break-even gross margins at December 31, 2022, and first delivery of the 777X-9 was revised in Q1 2022 from late 2023 to 2025.
These 787 and 777X disclosures are framed as program accounting, cost and certification-schedule matters; the 10-K does not describe them as litigation or claims.
raw_excerpt: In April 2022, we decided to pause production of the 777X-9 during 2022 and 2023. The production pause is resulting in abnormal production costs that are being expensed as incurred until 777X-9 production resumes. We expensed abnormal production costs of $325 during the year ended December 31, 2022. The 777X program has near break-even margins at December 31, 2022. ... The resulting reach-forward loss of $3,460 was recorded as a reduction to deferred production costs.

已知合同义务表列示：长期债务（含流动部分）575.35 亿美元、债务利息 336.63 亿美元、737 MAX 客户赔偿 7 亿美元（当期 1 亿、长期 6 亿）。
raw_excerpt: We expect to be able to fund our cash requirements through cash and short-term investments and cash provided by operations, as well as continued access to capital markets. At December 31, 2022, we had $14.6 billion of cash, $2.6 billion of short-term investments, and $12.0 billion of unused borrowing capacity on revolving credit line agreements. In the third quarter of 2022, we entered into a $5.8 billion 364-day revolving credit agreement expiring in August 2023, a $3 billion three-year revolving credit agreement expiring in August 2025, and amended our $3.2 [billion credit agreement].

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K, FY2022 — 风险因素与 MD&A: 债务规模、到期集中度与信用评级历史
key_points: 2022-12-31，Boeing 债务总额为 570 亿美元。
其中约 145 亿美元本金偿付将在未来三年内到期。
2022-12-31，飞机融资承诺总额为 161 亿美元。
公司称债务余额自 2019 年起显著上升，主因 737 MAX 停飞与 COVID-19 疫情影响。
公司债务余额上升导致 2020 年信用评级被下调，2021 年与 2022 年评级维持不变。
raw_excerpt: As of December 31, 2022, our debt totaled $57.0 billion of which approximately $14.5 billion of principal payments on outstanding debt will become due over the next three years. In addition, as of December 31, 2022, our airplane financing commitments totaled $16.1 billion. Our increased debt balance resulted in downgrades to our credit ratings in 2020, and our ratings remained unchanged in 2022 and 2021.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K, FY2022 — 风险因素: 保险覆盖充分性提示（无金额）
key_points: 公司提示其维持的保险金额可能不足以覆盖全部索赔或责任，可能被迫承担重大成本。
公司称其维持的保险覆盖可能不足以覆盖 737 MAX 事故相关或其他索赔与责任。
部分产品责任在美国境内受 2002 年《国土安全法》SAFETY Act 条款保护，但在美国境外无此保护，可能产生重大责任。
上述提示未给出任何保险覆盖金额或保险回收金额。
raw_excerpt: The amount of our insurance coverage may not cover all claims or liabilities, and we may be forced to bear substantial costs. ... While some of these products are shielded from liability within the U.S. under the SAFETY Act provisions of the 2002 Homeland Security Act, no such protection is available outside the U.S., potentially resulting in significant liabilities. ... The amount of insurance coverage we maintain may be inadequate to cover these or other claims or liabilities.
